clauses.finding: Extractable supplies an issued credential under a live label for each counted tag; proof knowledge soundness, unforgeability and group validation are obligations, not proved cryptography. Eligibility after a within-period withdrawal is not ensured merely by a live label.

tag is a deterministic function of secret and applicant identifier, with provenance assumed by Extractable. SecretStable supports one tag per member across labels. No unlinkability, public non-recomputability or cryptographic PRF claim is proved.

Distinct tags imply distinct Member values under Extractable and SecretStable; completeness additionally needs SecretFresh and TagInjective. This is a class-credential counting model, not established equivalence to every record profile or the Groth16 implementation.

Sequential spent-set acceptance counts a supplied value at most once; drip refuses one over-cap issuance batch. Scope/profile/interval authorization is delegated to an admissible Boolean and value encoding. Aggregate budget across issuers/batches, per-vetter attribution, idempotent acknowledgement, durable atomic concurrency and coupling spends to the attestation count are not modelled.

Applicant identifier a and secret aSec are separate parameters, with no derivation or possession relation between them. ApplicantSecret constrains credential secrets for the applicant Member only; it does not prove this holder-binding clause.

No transcriptDigest or complete submission binding is modelled. not_minted_refused checks a challenge against a supplied minted list and verification Boolean; single-use is a separate machine, not a transcript proof.

Member-level exclusion follows from Extractable secret inequality and ApplicantSecret. H-applicant can hold vacuously for an applicant with no class credential. Person-level self-vetting remains possible across Member identities; the Groth16 route has no established clause-7 correspondence.

clauses.finding: Leaf membership follows from path_sound under H-leaf, H-node and H-domain (record 001). The opening of L to (s, N; r) is modelled as L = com s N r; commitment binding (H-com) is a hypothesis used only by replacement_fixed, and hiding is outside the model.

Handle absence follows from neighbours_sound under H-sorted (record 006). The proof speaks for the stated epoch only (stale_root_passes in record 006 applies unchanged); revocation-list freshness is the verifier's.

With H-com and H-pre, one enrolment leaf admits exactly one replacement, so a holder of a stolen s can move the enrolment only to the committed L'. colliding_predigest_two_replacements shows H-pre is necessary. That the member can open L' is not established (does-not-establish 2).

The tag is a function of the secret, so a second rotation from the same secret repeats it and the spent-tag set refuses it (Spent.replay_refused). tag_not_nullifier proves issuance 3 under H-prf. PRF pseudorandomness and rotation unlinkability are computational and not modelled.
No transcriptDigest is modelled in R025; record 003 (swap_fails, digest_reduction_collides) applies by composition but is not proven here.
